name: hex glinski flanks
description: Glinski-style hexagonal chess on a native 91-cell hexagon, with promotion on the far edge, whose two empty flanks are joined. The upper-left and lower-right sides, the two flanks no army stands on, are one seam: a piece that leaves by one comes back in by the other, straight across, and either player may cross it either way. Every cell has six neighbours. A rook slides through the six edge neighbours, a bishop through the six cells that touch two of them, a queen does both, a king steps one cell in any of those twelve directions, and a knight leaps to the twelve nearest cells no rook or bishop line reaches. A pawn steps straight forward, two on its first move, and takes on the two neighbours either side of forward. A pawn that reaches the far edge, the eleven cells from which it has no step forward, becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight. There is no en passant and no castling. Each side has a king, a queen, two rooks, two knights, three bishops and nine pawns in a wedge. The second army is the first turned half a turn, so each king faces the other queen and each side promotes on the cells the other army started from. Checkmate wins; stalemate is a draw.

provenance.history: Schema 16's showcase for a hexagon's seams (Q281a4): the native twin hex-glinski-hexagon with rules.wrap {"nw_se": "both"}, joining file a's side to file k's, the pair no army stands on, so nothing crosses at ply 1. Pre-registered in docs/game-ideas.md: viable, ladder monotone, skill_gradient above 150, index within 0.05 of the parent's, and at least 0.5 of graded games containing a move across the seam. Measured in Q281d.
